title: Weight Wharf: orchestrated intake, conversion, and pin issuance for OSS LLMs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We frequently accept community-supplied model weights with heterogeneous formats (PyTorch, safetensors, HF sharded checkpoints) and varying metadata quality. The current intake flow is brittle: manual triage, ad-hoc conversion steps, and late-stage profiling leads to slow time-to-serve and intermittent runtime incompatibilities.

Goal: Implement an end-to-end orchestrator named 'Weight Wharf' that automates: secure weight intake, deterministic conversion into canonical runtime artifacts, signature and provenance verification, lightweight smoke validation, automated pin issuance (semantic version + compatibility metadata), and staged profile publish into the model catalog. The flow must be auditable, observable, and support manual intervention points.

Scope: This ticket covers the orchestration layer, CLI/controller tasks, conversion hooks, canonical artifact manifest generation, and the first-pass profile publish automation. It does NOT include low-level kernel selection logic or quantization engine implementation (those are separate components).

Non-goals: building new heavy quantization transforms, changing catalog UI, or adding enterprise billing integration in this iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Weight Wharf accepts three representative OSS checkpoints (one PyTorch .pt, one safetensors sharded, one HF 8-bit converted) and produces canonical runtime artifacts with consistent manifests.
Automated signature and checksum verification is performed; failing manifests are quarantined and a triage ticket created.
A deterministic conversion step (single command) produces identical artifacts across two different CI runs (byte-level manifest determinism for critical fields).
A lightweight smoke profile runner executes generation and perf micro-benchmarks (latency p95, peak memory, KV cache sanity) and produces a publishable performance profile in the catalog.
Pin issuance: canonical artifact published with a semantic model pin and compatibility matrix (supported runtimes/hardware/quantization modes).
End-to-end observability: each intake has traceable events in tracing system and token-level telemetry for the smoke runs appears in the Console dashboard.
Rollback: published profile can be reverted within 24 hours and triggers an automatic revert entry in the audit log.
Security: KMS-encrypted manifests and signed provenance metadata meet the security checklist and the security team has signed off (security_review_required true).
outcome_metrics: Reduce median time from weight receipt->catalog publish from current 5 days to <= 4 hours for standard cases.
Decrease manual triage volume for onboarding team by 60% in the first month.
First-week production compatibility failure rate <= 1% for models onboarded via Weight Wharf.
Publish coverage: at least 5 community models fully onboarded in the pilot week.
milestones: M1: Controller skeleton + secure intake endpoint (2026-03-08)
M2: Deterministic converter integration + smoke-run harness (2026-03-20)
M3: Pin issuance service + catalog publish API (2026-03-27)
M4: Pilot onboard 5 models and collect telemetry (2026-04-01)
M5: Security review and rollout playbook (2026-04-05)
implementation_notes: Intake model: S3 ingestion with signed upload URLs; manifest must include source_url, declared format, expected sha256, and provenance fields (uploader, commit-ish, license).
Conversion pipeline will invoke converter workers in a sandboxed container; each conversion run produces an immutable canonical artifact bundle + manifest.json + signature (edsig via KMS).
Determinism constraints: normalizing ordering of manifest fields, canonicalizing metadata keys, and including conversion toolchain version hash in output to ensure reproducible artifacts.
Smoke-run harness will be parallelizable and run on a small dedicated GPU pool (g4dn.xlarge equivalent) with a fixed prompt set and deterministic RNG seed.

Performance profile schema: latency p50/p95, tokens/sec under steady-state with batching=16, memory high-water mark, kv-cache growth curve, and a pass/fail set for generation correctness (sanity prompts).
Pin format: semantic model pin 'model-name@vYYYYMMDD.rN' plus a compatibility object (runtime tags, quantization-safe flags, recommended batch sizes).
Observability: emit structured events to x-trace with correlation_id=weight_wharf:<ingest_id> and attach smoke-run telemetry to the same trace.
Failure modes: on conversion failure create AUTO-Triage ticket with logs and attach a pre-signed support bundle; quarantined artifacts remain immutable until manual approve/reject.
test_plan: Unit tests around manifest normalization and signature verification.
Integration test: run full flow in staging with 3 canonical sample weights; assert artifact equality and profile publish existence.
Chaos test: simulate partial network failures during conversion and verify idempotent retry semantics.
Security test: verify KMS signing and access controls; run SCA on container images used for conversion.
Performance gate: smoke-run p95 latency must be within expected bound for at least 90% of runs.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: upstream weight manifests are missing license or provenance -> Mitigation: require manifest schema validation at intake and provide a dashed-line auto-notification to uploader with required fields.
Risk: conversion nondeterminism across runs -> Mitigation: pin converter docker image, record toolchain hashes, and add a deterministic post-processing normalization step.
Risk: bogus models that pass smoke but fail at scale -> Mitigation: staged rollout and production canary routing to a small percentage with automatic fallback to baseline models.
Risk: KMS rate limits during bulk onboarding -> Mitigation: batch signing requests and implement local ephemeral attestations cached for short TTL.
